title: Kirchhoff's first law and conservation of charge practice

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions cross the module boundary: q01 directly retrieves Lesson 3 and q07 mixes the current lesson with the verified Module 1 summary.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: immediate prior retrieval, conceptual junction diagnostics, direct current balance, multi-branch direction reasoning, then a mixed source-and-junction application

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, values and figures are original and do not reproduce mapped Cambridge questions.

questions.prompt: A discharging cell has e.m.f. E, internal resistance r and supplies current I. State the equation for its terminal potential difference V and explain what the term Ir represents.
Which statement is Kirchhoff's first law?

options.A: The sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum of currents leaving it.
options.B: The current is the same in every branch connected to a junction.
options.C: The sum of potential differences around a closed loop is zero.
options.D: The resistance of a junction equals the sum of its branch resistances.

questions.prompt: Why does Kirchhoff's first law apply at a junction in a steady circuit?

options.A: Electrical energy cannot be transferred in a branch.
options.B: Charge cannot be created, destroyed or continually stored at the junction.
options.C: Every branch must have the same resistance.
options.D: All charge carriers leave along the widest branch.
